question: Can a generative model explicitly learn and sample the full preimage of a fixed prediction by representing a many-to-one supervised task as locally label space times residual fiber space?

key_findings.claim: BundleNet reframes conditional generation as learning local trivializations of a supervised map, separating the specified output from residual input variation.
key_findings.evidence: The output space is clustered into neighborhoods. For each neighborhood, a conditioning code selects an invertible RealNVP-based map between input x and a pair (label y, latent fiber z). At generation time, fixing y and sampling z produces candidate inputs intended to lie in the fiber over y.

key_findings.claim: The fiber-bundle language is an inductive approximation, not a demonstrated topological property of the real data or a learned atlas with compatibility guarantees.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly caution that tasks should not be expected to form literal fiber bundles. Neighborhoods come from k-means or discrete labels, each chart is selected by its nearest representative, and training matches point-cloud distributions with prediction, nearest-neighbor KL, and minimum-distance losses. No transition maps, cocycle consistency, homeomorphism of data supports, or learned topology test is enforced.

key_findings.claim: On two synthetic surfaces and two low-dimensional tabular data sets, BundleNet usually has lower global and fiberwise sample discrepancy than the tested GAN baselines.
key_findings.evidence: For global Wasserstein-1, BundleNet is best in all four tables: 0.461 on torus, 0.264 on Mobius band, 1.733 on Wine Quality, and 1.448 on Airfoil Noise. It is also best in fiberwise Wasserstein-1 on three of four, with CGAN-local slightly better on Airfoil Noise, 3.076 versus 3.124. The appendix shows broadly similar but not completely uniform rankings across MSMD, MMD, two KL directions, W1, and W2.

key_findings.claim: Local batching and neighborhood conditioning explain part of the gain, so the experiments do not isolate topology, invertibility, and loss design as separate causes.
key_findings.evidence: CGAN-local, which receives the same neighborhood representative and restricts each batch to one neighborhood, is usually the strongest GAN and comes close or wins on Airfoil. CGAN-local-mixed degrades sharply. BundleNet still wins most metrics, but there are no ablations that independently remove invertibility, each loss term, chart conditioning, or local batching under matched capacity and tuning.

key_findings.claim: The apparent uncertainty bars quantify repeated sampling and metric evaluation for fixed trained models, not robustness across training seeds.
key_findings.evidence: Section 5.1 says generation and metric computation are repeated ten times and bootstrapped. Appendix Table 6 makes explicit that each configuration is trained once and evaluated repeatedly for a single set of weights. Consequently the narrow intervals do not measure optimizer variability, model-selection uncertainty, or baseline tuning variance.

key_findings.claim: The paper's fiberwise evaluation protocol is internally inconsistent and especially weak for continuous-output empirical data.
key_findings.evidence: Section 5.1 says 15 base points are sampled, while Appendix Table 10 says five. For synthetic data, 200 true fiber samples can be generated analytically; for real data the target is formed from available train-and-test points lying over a selected label. Continuous Airfoil labels need not provide a well-sampled conditional distribution at an exact y, and no effective fiber sample counts or conditional-neighborhood rule are reported.

key_findings.claim: Topological prior choice can matter on synthetic fibers, but topology is manually supplied rather than inferred or validated.
key_findings.evidence: A circular prior maps to an oval much better than one- or two-dimensional Gaussian choices and improves torus and Mobius metrics in Table 3. A sliced torus with fibers changing from a point to a circle shows that the model can approximate some non-bundle behavior but struggles near the singular fiber. On Airfoil Noise, varying circular priors has little effect.

key_findings.claim: The current implementation is confined to small low-dimensional problems by quadratic neighborhood losses and memory use.
key_findings.evidence: The authors identify O(n squared) nearest-neighbor KL computation, whole-neighborhood memory, and poor suitability for images as their main limitations. Experiments contain only 1,000-point synthetic surfaces plus Wine Quality and five-feature Airfoil Noise; every model trains for 2,000 epochs on one P100 GPU.

method.core_idea: Approximate a many-to-one supervised map with locally conditioned invertible networks whose coordinates are the desired output and a latent fiber variable, so fixing the output and varying the latent samples the preimage.
method.mechanism: Cluster continuous labels or use discrete label values to define base neighborhoods; assign one conditioning representative per neighborhood; construct a dimension-preserving conditional affine layer followed by alternating RealNVP blocks and permutations; train forward label reconstruction together with bidirectional nearest-neighbor KL and mean-squared-minimum-distance distribution losses; and invert the selected chart on pairs of a requested label and a sample from a hand-chosen mixed Gaussian or circular fiber prior.
assumptions: The supervised ground-truth relation from input to output is deterministic and measurable.
Within each selected neighborhood, the input distribution is usefully approximated by a product of output coordinates and one common fiber prior.
A nearest-centroid hard chart assignment is adequate near neighborhood boundaries.
Input dimension can be matched by the combined output and latent dimensions for an ambient invertible architecture.
The topology and dimension of the fiber prior can be chosen by the practitioner.
Nearest-neighbor KL and minimum-distance losses adequately measure conditional distribution coverage.
Low discrepancy against empirical points implies useful conditional or inverse-design samples.
The supervised labels used to select a chart are available at generation time.

techniques.role: Partitions label space into neighborhoods that act as approximate bundle charts.
Selects an invertible flow with a neighborhood representative.
Provides reversible affine coupling blocks between input and label-plus-fiber coordinates.
Encodes residual variation with manually chosen Gaussian and circular latent factors.
Matches generated and target point clouds in both KL directions using nearest-neighbor density estimates.
Penalizes generated points that lie far from an empirical neighborhood.

evaluations.setting: Torus and Mobius-band point clouds embedded in three dimensions with known base and fibers.
evaluations.metric: Global and fiberwise MSMD, MMD, forward and backward KL, Wasserstein-1, and Wasserstein-2.
evaluations.result: BundleNet is best across the reported headline W1 comparisons and visually preserves fiber organization better than the GAN baselines.
evaluations.baseline: Wasserstein-divergence GAN for global generation, conditional GAN, and neighborhood-conditioned CGAN-local.

evaluations.setting: Wine Quality with 11 inputs and categorical color-quality output, and Airfoil Noise with five inputs and one continuous target.
evaluations.metric: Distances between 4,000 global samples or empirical fiberwise point sets and generated samples.
evaluations.result: BundleNet wins every global W1 comparison and Wine fiberwise W1; CGAN-local slightly wins Airfoil fiberwise W1, with several other Airfoil metrics similarly close.
evaluations.baseline: WGAN, CGAN, and CGAN-local trained for the same 2,000 epoch count.

evaluations.setting: Prior-topology study mapping Gaussian or circular latent samples to an oval and retraining synthetic BundleNets.
evaluations.metric: Visual convergence and global or fiberwise Wasserstein-1.
evaluations.result: The circular prior fits the oval and improves both torus and Mobius results, while the Airfoil ablation is comparatively insensitive to the number of circular factors.
evaluations.baseline: One- and two-dimensional Gaussian priors and zero to six circular factors.

evaluations.setting: A sliced torus whose fibers change continuously from a point to a circle and back.
evaluations.metric: Six global and fiberwise point-cloud discrepancies plus visual reconstruction.
evaluations.result: BundleNet retains a recognizable distribution and favorable metrics but shows difficulty at the singular point-fiber, demonstrating flexibility beyond a strict bundle without establishing general singular-fiber handling.
evaluations.baseline: The ordinary torus and visual WGAN, CGAN, and CGAN-local reconstructions.

evaluations.setting: One to 100 label-space neighborhoods on the torus.
evaluations.metric: Global and fiberwise Wasserstein-1 from one trained model per configuration.
evaluations.result: Fiberwise W1 improves dramatically from one to two charts but has no monotonic gain thereafter; global W1 changes little.
evaluations.baseline: A single global chart versus increasingly fine k-means partitions.

limitations: Author-stated: real tasks need not be fiber bundles on the nose; the framework is a local product approximation.
Author-stated: the nearest-neighbor KL implementation is quadratic in neighborhood size and memory-heavy.
Author-stated: the current architecture is not well suited to image data or other high-dimensional inputs.
Author-stated: fiber prior topology and neighborhood count require practitioner choices and experimentation.
Reviewer inference: local flows are not coupled by transition-map or overlap-consistency constraints, so they do not learn a mathematical bundle atlas.
Reviewer inference: narrow bootstrap intervals condition on one set of trained weights and omit training-seed and hyperparameter-selection uncertainty.
Reviewer inference: the paper conflicts on whether fiberwise evaluation uses 15 or five base points.
Reviewer inference: empirical continuous-output fibers can contain too few exact-label observations to support a 200-sample conditional reference, and effective sample sizes are not given.
Reviewer inference: baseline tuning, capacity, adversarial stability, and loss design are not matched closely enough to attribute gains uniquely to fiber-bundle structure.
Reviewer inference: no downstream inverse-design success, uncertainty calibration, physical constraint, or out-of-distribution test is reported.
Reviewer inference: invertibility in ambient Euclidean coordinates does not itself guarantee a homeomorphism between the learned and true data supports.
failure_modes: A requested label lies near a hard chart boundary and two neighboring flows generate discontinuous conditional distributions.
The chosen latent fiber has the wrong topology, forcing tears, folds, density collapse, or off-manifold samples.
Fiber topology changes with y and a fixed local prior fails near a singular or bifurcation point.
A rare conditional mode is absent from the empirical neighborhood and the minimum-distance loss rewards its omission.
The inverse flow is mathematically defined but numerically unstable, producing exploding samples outside the training support.
A low point-cloud distance hides violation of the requested label when the forward prediction loss is imperfect.
K-means neighborhoods follow label density rather than the geometry needed for valid local trivialization.
Quadratic neighborhood computation makes training infeasible before image-scale or scientific inverse-design performance can be tested.
reusable_insights: Evaluate conditional generators fiberwise; strong global distribution metrics can conceal failure to preserve the conditioning map.
Local charts can remove topological obstructions that a single global Euclidean latent map cannot represent.
Invertible coordinates of the form observed output plus residual latent provide a transparent template for sampling ambiguous inverse solutions.
Topology choice should be treated as a falsifiable model-selection problem rather than decorative geometric terminology.
Chart overlaps need explicit consistency losses if locally trained conditional generators are expected to form one coherent global object.
Report training-seed variation separately from Monte Carlo variation of samples drawn from a fixed generator.
Real inverse-design benchmarks need conditional coverage, constraint satisfaction, diversity, and downstream utility, not only unconditional transport distances.
open_questions: Can fiber dimension and topology be inferred from data with uncertainty rather than manually specified?
How should transition maps and cocycle consistency be learned across overlapping conditional charts?
Can scalable sliced, kernel, or score-based objectives replace the quadratic nearest-neighbor KL loss?
How can fiberwise goodness be estimated for continuous labels when each exact empirical preimage has one or very few observations?
Would conditional diffusion, flow matching, or modern conditional normalizing flows outperform BundleNet under matched tuning and compute?
Can a chart system adapt around singular fibers, bifurcations, disconnected components, and varying topology?
Do generated fibers produce valid, diverse, and experimentally confirmed inverse designs in materials or physics?
Which numerical constraints prevent exploding inverses while preserving expressive local topology at high dimension?

competitive_landscape.title: Analyzing Inverse Problems with Invertible Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Ardizzone and colleagues already learn a joint invertible map from parameters to measurements plus latent variables and sample ambiguous inverse solutions by fixing a measurement and varying the latent. BundleNet's clearest addition is the explicit local-chart and fiber-bundle framing, neighborhood conditioning, and topology-aware latent study, so its claim to introduce the underlying many-to-one sampling task should be read narrowly.

competitive_landscape.title: SurVAE Flows: Surjections to Bridge the Gap between VAEs and Flows
competitive_landscape.difference: SurVAE Flows make many-to-one and stochastic inverse transformations explicit composable layers with likelihood accounting. BundleNet instead augments a supervised output with a fiber latent to restore local bijectivity and optimizes point-cloud losses rather than a general surjective likelihood framework.

competitive_landscape.title: Multi-Chart Flows
competitive_landscape.difference: Kalatzis and colleagues use multiple coordinate charts to learn distributions on topologically nontrivial manifolds. Their target is unconditional manifold density, while BundleNet specializes charts to a supervised many-to-one map and conditional fibers; both rely on locality to avoid one global Euclidean parameterization.

competitive_landscape.title: Fiber Bundle Morphisms as a Framework for Modeling Many-to-Many Maps
competitive_landscape.difference: Coda and colleagues extend the same fiber-bundle program to stochastic many-to-many relations using bundle morphisms and test against conditional GANs and conditional normalizing flows. It broadens BundleNet's deterministic ground-truth map but remains a small synthetic workshop study rather than a high-dimensional validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Universal Joint Approximation of Manifolds and Densities by Simple Injective Flows
competitive_landscape.difference: Puthawala and colleagues characterize when injective flows can jointly approximate embedded manifolds and densities and prove that embedding dimension controls topological obstructions. BundleNet supplies an empirical local conditional construction but no analogous approximation or topology-recovery theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding and Mitigating Exploding Inverses in Invertible Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Behrmann and colleagues show that nominally invertible architectures can become numerically non-invertible and fail at sampling or change-of-variables calculations. BundleNet relies on inverse evaluation but does not report bi-Lipschitz control, conditioning diagnostics, or out-of-distribution inverse stability.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning geometry and topology via multi-chart flows
competitive_landscape.difference: Yu and colleagues give a general multi-flow gluing scheme and algorithms for geometry and topology estimation, showing significant topology-recovery gains over a single flow. This advances the chart-consistency and learned-topology questions that BundleNet leaves to manually selected neighborhoods and priors.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: BundleNet introduces the task of modeling supervised-map fibers and a topology-inspired generative architecture whose local trivializations outperform popular GANs on synthetic and real data.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper defines a fiberwise task, builds neighborhood-conditioned RealNVP maps with label and residual coordinates, reports six discrepancy metrics over four data sets, and probes neighborhood count, latent topology, and varying fiber topology.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest contribution is a lucid local-chart formulation and an evaluation that exposes how global generative quality can miss conditional-fiber failure. Invertible inverse-problem networks already implement the core output-plus-latent construction, and contemporary multi-chart and surjective-flow work covers adjacent geometry. The experiments make BundleNet promising for small point clouds, but one-trained-model intervals, an inconsistent fiberwise protocol, limited baselines, and no chart-gluing or high-dimensional result prevent a general claim that the method learns fiber bundles or solves practical inverse design.
